speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In Singapore, there is one element of these four that has pervaded all aspects of our recent history, politics, policies, lives and perhaps even our future, and that is housing.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Fifty-seven years later, we need to look further ahead to uphold the housing priority.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I call it the "Up, Down, Left-Right and All around".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While we cleared cemeteries and backfilled mudflats to create living space over the years and build new towns, the question is: how much more and where?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Eventually, we will reach a point of saturation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Selective En bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS) we can do selectively, but at greater cost.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, therefore, ask the Ministry to look to the far horizon, identify future sites early – be they greenfield sites, reclaimed sites, SERS sites – inform early, consult early, discuss widely, and plan prudently.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What does the next 10 years look like for Build-To-Order (BTO) supply as well as public rental housing?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What has previous economic downturns taught us about the housing market?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As blocks go up, concerns about affordability also go up too.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We often trot out examples of how families earning about $1,000 can afford a flat.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But for many lower-income Singaporeans facing complex issues, it is still elusive for them.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Middle-income families also fear that their incomes are not keeping pace with the rising cost of housing as well as the cost of living.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, therefore, ask and seek the Ministry's reassurance to Singaporeans that public housing prices will be kept stable and affordable for the majority, especially young families starting out.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As the economy slows, there is also the added fear that retrenchments may rise and loans defaulted.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Next, "Left and Right", broadening our overall choices.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew once said that "If every family owned its home, the country would be more stable".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The stability that we have today also challenges us to look beyond homes just for the masses.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Today, many of our elderly are asset rich.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This seems like a very low take-up rate as 75% of elderly households are eligible.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Is it a matter of publicity and awareness?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On my house visits, many older residents whom I speak to are unaware of the scheme.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Good schemes like this cannot be hidden away.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, we need to do more to promote it.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, of course, also have a significant number of elderly 5-roomers in my estate.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many of them have asked about the scheme and so I would like to appeal for, over the long term, an eventual Enhanced Enhanced Scheme for them.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Homes are aspirational after all; it gives us stability and grounding.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am glad that the Finance Minister announced the quantum for the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Before formal announcement of the details, I would like to make a number of recommendations based on families that I have met and interacted with.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We need to make sure that the Fresh Start Housing Scheme has a good start and not end up with a false start.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Let us help rental families move out of rental into home ownership and give them a leg up for their future while keeping costs down for them.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The next step in the housing landscape is to build communities, rather than just building houses.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The kampong spirit of the past is not easily translatable from horizontal kampong to the vertical ones that we have today.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Community space must be deliberately planned to create circulation for residents to meet, greet, interact and bond.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To this end, new towns should have this as a basic planning parameter, integrate facilities and different flat types, work early to create opportunities to form communities of support.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For older towns, I also urge that the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) be expanded and made a staple of the revitalisation of towns with a focus on building communities.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I spoke about my concerns over the Revitalisation of Shop Scheme in the Budget debate which I hope the Ministry will also address.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Shops and services make community possible, but a simple paint job does not make town centres come alive again, especially with the competition from malls.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Such a policy would also have impacts across other policies.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We need to work together to build better homes with Singaporeans, for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Otherwise, there will be negative impact on real estate related industries such as construction, interior design, renovation contractors, furniture and consumer electrical and electronics, which, in turn, affect jobs.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Housing affordability must remain a top priority, especially for our first-timer families.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For most young Singaporean couples, they must have their own homes first before they proceed to have children.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Hence, with our birth rate hinging on our housing policy, HDB must ensure that we make available plenty of nests to welcome the stork.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should have a wide range of flats for every budget and need.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Wherever possible, public and private housing, even public rental blocks, should be integrated in each estate to facilitate community bonding.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For the most vulnerable of our households, I hope the Ministry will be able to accommodate them quickly to reduce the anxiety for the elderly and children in their midst.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our home buyers have benefited from recent enhancements to the income ceiling and housing grants, but individual choices, such as the preference for housing in mature estates and proximity to family members, pose challenges for buyers and HDB.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One of the solutions is to build our new estates even better to attract these home buyers and their families.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These new estates must have the full range of facilities, well-designed and well-integrated with the surrounding ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They have shared public spaces, barrier-free accessibility and better connectivity for pedestrians and cyclists and are visually appealing.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For home buyers purchasing homes in mature estates so as to be nearer to their families, HDB also provides housing grants as the resale prices of these flats are higher than direct purchases from HDB.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the lease gets shorter, it will eventually lead to declining HDB flat values which will affect retirement planning.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To further protect against the declining HDB flat values for older estates, would there be the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) schemes for flats built after 1986 after the completion of the current HIP in 2018?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Government consider putting an upper limit on the pricing of each type of EC unit or limiting the type of frills which can be included in the development plot so as to ensure that EC flats will always remain affordable?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Increasingly, many couples are getting married later due to the pursuit of higher education and work commitments.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: By the time they meet their other half and get married, their combined income would have exceeded the income ceiling.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope we can give every couple a chance to own and live in an HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, it may not be a bad idea to have a few more families with higher incomes live within an HDB estate.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There should be more opportunities for people of different income groups interacting with one another for better community bonding.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Removing the income ceiling could improve social integration and enhance social stability.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: HDB may consider selling flats to those with higher incomes with reduced subsidies.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, I would like to appeal to the Ministry to consider giving third-timer applicants another opportunity to buy their own flats.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some of these applicants might have run into financial difficulties or have personal problems which result in them having to sell their flats.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A number of these applicants could have been co-owners for their parents' flats because their parents could not afford or run into difficulties servicing their mortgages.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Later, when these applicants get married, they would be considered second-timers, and by the time they wanted to upgrade or downgrade, they would be considered third-timers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Ministry consider allowing them to do so, subject to the restriction that they can only sell the flat back to HDB?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Singapore is often credited for its successful housing policy.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In particular, we should help the low-income families with young children secure home ownership.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These will be more affordable for the low-income families.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Those who are currently living in public rental flats would prefer to own their own flats eventually.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Families with low incomes struggle to secure mortgages.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is especially difficult for second-timer families that are not eligible for the more generous first-timer grants and concessionary loans under HDB.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These families should be given a second chance to secure a home.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Of course, measures should be put in place to prevent people from profiteering off this scheme.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Furthermore, the Government should look into the reasons these families sold their first flats in the first place.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instance, if the family had sold their first flat to pay off the gambling debts of a problem gambler within the family, then this problem gambler should be identified and referred to specialists for help so that history would not repeat itself.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: While affordability is a function of supply and demand, but for some families, this is not merely about the price of a flat.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For some, this is a welcome move as it will enable them and their families to start afresh.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, there are others who, though desire to have a place of their own, may have other considerations that deter them from making the purchase.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Some of the considerations include flat locations, whether they can purchase their existing rental flats, upfront cash payment, shorter lease period and so on.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Some families have school-going children or preschoolers already enrolled in nearby childcare centres.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: If they have to move to flats located far from their current rental place, the availability of suitable schools and childcare to transfer their children into will be a key priority for them, without which, they may not be able to continue working and have care support for their children.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As such, some may prefer to purchase their existing 2-room rental flat.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: And how will the proportion of rental versus sale flats in such blocks or areas be managed in the long run?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: A number of these eligible families may have difficulties having sufficient cash for the downpayment of the flat.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Given that flats of this nature may have a shorter lease period, the possibility of resale for such flats after the minimum occupation period (MOP), assuming MOP is longer than five years, unlike in a BTO or the regular direct sale flats, will become less attractive.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This will actually discourage some families to take up the scheme as they would be concerned that their investment in such flats will not ensure they can afford a home during their retirement.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I suggest that the Ministry consider further what more can be done to address the aforementioned points.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This may be helpful for those young families who wish to live closer to their parents and want to have a flat sooner than BTO flats or have been repeatedly unsuccessful in the sale of balance flats exercise.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The results would be a win-win solution where they have better extended support from their parents and are also able to start a family earlier at a lower cost.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: What is the definition of a sustainable and connected town in a developed city?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The answer can vary widely depending on who we ask and people's expectations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For a developed city, continuous planning, creation and renewal efforts need to be in place for new towns and mature towns.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: First, the planning horizon has to take a longer-term perspective for better integration of the old and new towns, to prevent fragmented developments as we move from one town to another.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Second, renewal of old towns must be sustainable.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Thus, designs must be practical for maintenance and yet aesthetically lasting.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Third, basic amenities and infrastructures to support new developments have to be built in tandem, rather than as add-ons or an afterthought.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Lastly, connectivity between and within townships has a broader implication beyond just transportation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Planning of new towns, in some aspects, is easier than in mature towns as requirements can be designed in to meet the needs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For mature towns, direct or simple modifications may not necessarily be possible at times to achieve the same outcome as in a new town.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In such instances, master planning for purposes of land use and land sale should have systems in place for early notification and enable integration or adaption of feedback from local communities.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Co-development would increase acceptance from the local communities and allow better collaboration.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In fitting amenities for public usage, sometimes, it is easy to forget the pragmatic need for maintenance and ease of upgrading.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: So, from material selection and design to ergonomics, it is important to fully consider all aspects before the build.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: This will help to ensure practicality, functionality and better cost management of common amenities in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As estates begin to mature and are more built-up with time, it is inconvenient to bear with the modifications that are required to cope with the capacity, but this is understandably acceptable as it is necessary.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, moving forward, I hope that the need for integrated planning, design and executing solutions ahead to manage potential practical challenges of a developed living community is an area that the inter-agencies can consider and improve upon.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: In our efforts to improve connectivity, much of the focus has been put on connecting and moving people through transportation.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We emphasise on the availability of hardware and timeliness of putting them in place, but very often, lacking is a fundamental thought around how users could actually be integrated into the process as infrastructures are being made available over time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: An example would be cycling as we strive to be car-lite.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I think cyclists and pedestrians both have a right of way on shared pavements.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Faisal Manap, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Deprived of a permanent shelter and essential human needs, it has a direct negative impact on the well-being of the affected individual, as well as our society at large.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: To date, I have on several occasions, raised the problem of homelessness in our midst.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I, like many Members in this House, have also personally attended to a number of cases and it is certainly a heartbreaking process to see our fellow Singaporeans being left without a place where they can call home.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I understand that this issue of homelessness is a multifaceted and complex one, a problem that requires the assistance of several stakeholders, including the affected individual and his family.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As a Member of this House, I would like to share my observations and put forward proposals to better mitigate this issue and bring some comfort to our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In a previous reply by MSF to my Parliamentary Question, the House was informed that in 2014, a study on families in transitional housing was conducted and it was found that these families often experienced occurrences, such as divorce and financial difficulties.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In fact, many had sold their flats and spent their monies to clear existing debts or for other purposes, prior to becoming homeless.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is argued that home owners will benefit from the sales proceeds, but as many Members of this House would concur, some home owners are left without much cash proceeds after clearing their personal debts and arrears, arising from personal circumstances or legal rulings.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As such, we need to have a more strategic and systemic manner in which we can capture the most vulnerable in our midst, especially those who potentially face a higher risk of being homeless after the sale of a flat, such as the elderly and families with young children.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: A proactive and flexible approach to the implementation of the 13-month rule would certainly be comforting to many, akin to the spirit as expressed in the Chinese proverb "sending warm coal in the midst of a harsh winter".

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As the family nucleus in Singapore shrinks in size, help should be given to elderly owners to use their flats to supplement their retirement income, without requiring them to move out.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: One is the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS), a monetisation scheme to help elderly households in 3-room or smaller flats unlock their housing equity.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The other, often suggested by the Ministry, is the sub-letting of a bedroom in the existing household.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: There are many issues involved in the execution of the latter option.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It could range from the infringement of personal space to elderly owners facing difficulties obtaining tenants without the engagement of a real estate agent.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Engaging a real estate agent could constitute an added financial burden on our elderly when, in the first place, they already do not have much for retirement to begin with.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This could encourage up to two-fifths of elderly owners to sublet their flats to support their retirement.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: We can and must do so much more for our elderly Singaporeans who have toiled to transform Singapore to what it is today.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: Since last year, the Ministry has enhanced the scheme in various ways to improve the take-up rate.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: And significantly, to allow them to buy this back at the price of the unit, valued at the time the LBS was executed by their parents.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: I believe this will help address the concern on the part of elderly parents that their children will not be able to inherit the flat from them and hence, would not enjoy that financial benefit to help them cope with the higher property prices in the future.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: These seniors worry that property in the future may be unaffordable to their children, especially those who do not currently own flats.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: They wish to pass on to their children, as much as possible, the value that has accrued to their flats over the years, less, of course, the amount of financial support that the seniors expect to receive from the lease buy out.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: This could well result in their children acquiring their property at below market rates in the future, but this is no different from parents passing on their property to their children – an accepted principle.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: All that changes here is that those seniors who are in need will get another option to monetise their flats now, while their children may be unable or even unwilling to provide for them in full.

speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
text: But still, as parents, they wish to offer better protection to their children from future property price inflation, a concern that may now be holding them back from taking up the LBS.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am sure our Government remains committed to aiding low-income and vulnerable households to achieve this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some families cannot afford to own their flat due to some difficulties.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, they have to take a public rental flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I sympathise a lot with divorcees with children.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Having to go through divorce is already very painful.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What more, if they have to shift out of their matrimonial home?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Without a roof over their head, they will have difficulty deciding which school to send their children to.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Single parents are particularly stressed in such situations because they are often the sole breadwinner and caregiver of their children.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can special priority be given to those divorcees with children or those in the process of going through a divorce to get a flat?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Administrative red tape only contributes further to their predicament.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are we able to expedite the approval process?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Last but not least, it is those who applied for new BTO flats under the singles scheme.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have heard quite a lot of feedback from my residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They told me that they had applied many times.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, can the Ministry build more 2-room flats for singles so that they can get their flats faster?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is the current building plan for this category?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Ten years ago when I first came to Nee Soon South, residents would always ask me when I was walking around in the constituency, "MP, when are you going to help renovate my lift?" Now, 10 years later, as I walk around in the constituency, residents will always say to me: "Aiyo, I am getting old.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My house is run-down and the toilet is falling apart.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When are you going to help me renovate my toilet?" What they are referring to is the Home Improvement Programme (HIP).

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Every day, my residents hope that HIP can be accelerated to benefit them as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, I hope that the authorities can do more and do faster.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While home ownership rates have been traditionally high compared to other countries, there are still some Singaporeans who are unable to afford flats and count on HDB to provide rental housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Most Singaporeans who need this rental housing have no other immediate alternatives and, as such, need the housing urgently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Some may be able to rent rooms in the open market in the short term but, with high rental rates, these further cripple their already dire financial situation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Next, Madam, as a small country with limited land, the Government is rightly continuing our expansion of affordable and reliable public transportation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, beyond public transportation, I hope we can also focus on expanding our cycling track network in our efforts of becoming a car-lite city.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, how can we better support the use of bicycles for transportation between homes and MRT stations or bus interchanges, and between MRT stations or bus interchanges to workplaces?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Low-income, vulnerable households and young families waiting for their BTO flats require more help in securing temporary housing.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There should be greater empathy for single parents, and second- and third-time HDB loan applicants who may be compelled by circumstances to move, such as having to downsize their homes for financial reasons.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Whether it is to start afresh or to start a new family, stability and insecurity are important influencing factors.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: That usually means being able to settle down in a place to call their own.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Fresh Start Housing Scheme is a thoughtful scheme that gives low-income households hope to progress into home ownership.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Unemployment is a common problem in vulnerable households and probably one of the main reasons a family would have to rely on this scheme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some single parents are in transition, for example, and I have residents who are newly divorced homemakers who would require some time to get their children settled in and then find a job, which would be another hurdle.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In our pursuit of a car-lite city, travel efficiency and connectivity must also be improved so that citizens do not find the need to rely on their own transport to get around.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: New towns must be designed with better connectivity, while mature estates should have their infrastructure enhanced.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Masterplan for HealthCity Novena is highly inspiring in this respect, for it will physically link Tan Tock Seng Hospital, the medical school and all public and volunteer healthcare facilities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This mirrors my expectations of a well-connected estate, which not only facilitates greater ease of travel and convenient access of amenities, but also brings neighbours physically closer together.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It would be ideal if agencies could work together and come up with a design master plan that fully integrates the residential areas with amenities and public transport through a network of linkways.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Louis Ng talks about the need for more bike rental options, possibly in town and residential areas as well.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But I think more needs to be done to support the overall cycling infrastructure, as dedicated cycling routes that have been designed with cyclists in mind should be considered to better connect our towns to the city.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat talks about the design of HDB towns, and I agree that URA should work with HDB and other agencies to build a car-free, pro-cycling and also pro-pedestrian network.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The ideal scenario for such new towns would be entire vehicle-free zones where residents can walk, cycle and scoot as they go about their activities.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In many ways, Singapore is an ideal market for EVs, with low driving distances and high petrol taxes.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: By some estimates, it is already economical to own an EV, relative to more traditional internal combustion engine vehicles, and, with battery costs falling, this will increase in the future.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore is uniquely positioned to avoid the biggest obstacle to kick-starting EV adoption, which is the need to build a dense public charging network, as home charging would be sufficient for the majority of users.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, more than 90% of Singaporeans live in high-rise homes and hence, currently do not have the right to install the required charge points in their common carparks, be they HDB or condominiums.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Hence, they could not get an EV even if they wanted to.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Many shoppers, local and international, had to brave the rain to walk from Paragon to 313 Orchard to catch the MRT train.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This is not quite acceptable if we want to make Orchard Road a world-class premier shopping belt.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Neither does it gel well with the Ministry of Transport's (MOT) big push for the walk-and-ride scheme.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In response to my Parliamentary Question last month, the Minister for National Development replied that URA only requires building owners to build linkways on new developments or when existing developments undergo major upgrading.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: As there were only a few developments or redevelopments along Orchard Road in the past 10 years, the progress of building underground linkways has been quite slow.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I hope that MND can re-look the existing policy and take the lead in building overhead and underground pedestrian linkways along Orchard Road, so that shoppers can shop in comfort and be shielded from the elements along the stretch of Orchard Road from Ion Orchard right up to Plaza Singapura.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The drivers of these vehicles would park along the road because parking is free.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the morning, the drivers would collect their vehicles and then go about their business.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Although the vehicles are not classified as heavy vehicles which require a heavy vehicle parking certificate, many of these vehicles are large commercial vehicles.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Residents are also concerned that there are total strangers parking just outside their homes.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair again at 4.20 pm.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.00 pm until 4.20 pm.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When I came to MND last year, many people told me I was going to a hot seat and wished me good luck.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, housing has always been a hot-button issue, and as I was preparing for this Committee of Supply (COS) debate, which is my first COS for MND, I went back to the Hansard to look at the records of previous years' debates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, from the start of our housing programme, going back to the 1960s, there have been lively debates on the MND Budget and on housing issues.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is no different this year, if you look at the number of cuts we received.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Here, I would like to acknowledge the work of the MND team, especially the HDB officials who have worked very hard to ramp up our building programme over the past few years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I also want to recognise all who have partnered us in this effort – our consultants, contractors, construction workers, as well as the many members of public who participated in our focus groups to give us feedback and help shape our policies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I think this demonstrates the importance of partnerships in the work we do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It applies not just to public housing and HDB, but also to the rest of our MND work, including our other Statutory Boards – the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority (AVA), Building and Construction Authority (BCA), Council of Estate Agencies (CEA), National Parks Board (NParks) and URA.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a common thread across all that we do in MND, about building a better home in partnership with Singaporeans and for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Mr Alex Yam said, it ultimately is about building communities, and it is our people who shape our sense of community and our sense of home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why over the past years, we have stepped up our engagement with Singaporeans to "inform early, consult early, discuss widely", as suggested by Mr Yam.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We did this with "Our Singapore Conversation" in 2013, continued with engagements on public housing over the past two years.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started our SGFuture dialogues this year to shape our next phase of development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, I will share some of the key priorities we have identified for MND based on these engagements.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we will strengthen our home ownership programme to meet the needs of Singaporeans, especially the more vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will transform our urban landscape to invest in new infrastructure for our future economy and to build a future city that we can be proud of.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we will create a quality living environment for all to enjoy and make Singapore a more car-lite and people-friendly city.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has always been the hallmark of our public housing system and we must and will continue to strengthen this key pillar of our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our focus is to help young couples own their first flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we enhanced our housing grants last year, and since then, many more homebuyers have benefited.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One such couple is Mr See Cheng Long and his fiancée Miss Felicia Poh.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, they were able to buy the flat for less than $140,000.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This meant that the mortgage loan was completely paid for or will be completely paid for using their CPF.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is no need for any cash outlay and so they end up having more savings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope this gives them confidence to plan for the next step – to get married and hopefully start a family soon.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our housing subsidies are rightly focused on the lower and middle-income households, but we have not neglected those in the higher income groups as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, we increased the income ceiling to enable more households at the higher end to buy a subsidised flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested that we do away with the income ceiling altogether.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I appreciate his intent to allow all Singaporeans to buy an HDB flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is something we would like to do as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to move in this direction and that is why the income ceiling has been progressively moved up over time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, I want to assure Mr Gan that we will continue to take steps to ensure that Executive Condominiums (ECs) remain affordable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We already do so through various measures and that is why ECs today, are more affordable than comparable private properties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, if you look back over the past few quarters, EC prices have remained relatively stable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to monitor and take necessary action if needed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides housing grants, we have also shortened the queues considerably for first-timers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One measure of this is the application rate of first-timer families for new BTO flats in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In practice, it means that most will be able to select their new BTO flat within their first or second application, and definitely on their third try.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand Members have shared concerns about newlywed couples who have repeatedly applied for an HDB flat without success.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have heard similar experiences during my Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, one couple told me at MPS that they had applied more than five times!

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I went back to HDB and asked for a check.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I found out that they were, in fact, interested in flats near the city centre and so all their applications were for flats in mature estates around the city centre, for example, in Ang Mo Kio and Toa Payoh.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have already announced that HDB will offer more flats in mature estates this year.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we have new projects in Bidadari and Tampines North.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is a physical limit to how much more we can build in these already developed areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I would encourage first-timer couples to consider applying for flats in non-mature estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I have mentioned earlier, if you look at the application rate, there is a very high chance of them getting it within their first and second try, and definitely within their third try.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the flats, in these estates are also more affordable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While waiting for the flats to be completed, they can consider renting a flat under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recognise that some want a flat more urgently or would prefer specific locations for good and practical reasons, for example, to live near their parents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the current market, they can consider buying a resale flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Resale prices have moderated and are more affordable now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we can compare HDB resale prices against household income.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At one time, prices were rising faster than income.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, housing affordability has improved and there are many attractive options available in the resale market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked if we can do more to help young married couples to get their flats early and live nearer to parents.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I share her desire to do so and we will continue to study ways to help them further.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also managed to reduce the queue for second-timer families and they, too, can benefit from the Proximity Grant.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Here, I would like to share the experience of one couple, Mdm Nur Liza binte Roslan and Mr Yulandi bin Abu Bakar.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They bought their first flat which was a 4-room flat at Taman Jurong from HDB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As their family grew, Mdm Nur Liza wanted to move out and move closer to her parents who are living in Bukit Batok so that they can help look after the children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is, in fact, comparable to what they would have had to pay for a new 4-room flat from HDB as second-timers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, they are better off by going to the resale market.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The amount they pay is about the same as a BTO after the grant.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They get a flat closer to their parents and get to move in earlier as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, for both first timers and second timers, the softening of the property market and the introduction of the new Proximity Grant and enhancements of all the various grant that we have had mean that there are many more attractive options to consider for purchasing a home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, there are also more housing options for singles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In 2013, we made a significant policy shift to allow first-timer singles to buy a new 2-room flat from HDB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, the BTO application rate among singles has been steadily improving.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I intend to bring down this application rate further.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will take time, but we will make it happen.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The move to open new flats to singles is a significant one and has met with a strong demand surge.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will need some time to clear the bulk of this demand, but we will bring down the application rate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In considering their home options, home buyers will have to do their homework, and they should evaluate carefully the different factors before making the purchase.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong mentioned one concern about the lease of existing flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He is right that, like all leasehold properties, the value of an HDB flat will decline as leases run down.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Flat buyers and home buyers have to take this into account in their financial planning.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for now, a large majority of flats have more than 60 years of lease remaining.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They continue to be highly liveable and the neighbourhoods will benefit from upgrading from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is still value in our resale flats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to find ways to help our elderly Singaporeans monetise the value of their flats in an orderly fashion and we will also publicise the schemes for doing so, as Members like Mr Alex Yam, Mr Faisal Manap and Mr Chen Show Mao have highlighted.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister of State Koh Poh Koon will elaborate on this later in his speech.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: My message to home buyers is this: we will do whatever we can to support you in your home ownership goals.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But please choose a home that meets your needs and is within your means.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand the desire to buy a large flat or one with a central location, but this should not come at the expense of a huge debt burden overwhelming the entire family.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Having cleared the backlog for first timers and made progress for singles and second timers, we are now getting more requests for new flats to accommodate other buyer groups.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested giving Singaporeans the chance to buy a third BTO flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand why people would like to buy a new flat from HDB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are allowing them to do so twice.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also have short-lease 2-room flexi flats for seniors to buy a third flat from HDB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I do not think we can go beyond that.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To allow a "third bite of the housing cherry" for all is not sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our land is limited; our financial resources are finite.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must, therefore, prioritise among various home buyers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is easy to give in to the demands and accommodate all the immediate requests and build as much as we can today and not think about tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this would not be a responsible thing to do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must consider the impact of our actions today on the next generation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must always be mindful of the implications of over-building and consider how a glut of flats will have a negative impact on the value of homes for all Singaporeans So, we need to strike that balance.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is more than the previous year, and we have done so to accommodate the increased demand from recent policy changes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, we are monitoring the property market very closely.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members spoke about this and called for a lifting of the cooling measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza mentioned this earlier in the Budget debate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Alex Yam and Mr Chong Kee Hiong suggested this earlier as well.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is too early to declare victory and unwind the measures.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Any relaxation of the measures now may risk a premature market rebound and I am sure that is an outcome we all want to avoid.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nevertheless, we recognise that the property market is affected by the broader economy and global events.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also very mindful that the property market, in turn, can have a broader impact on other sectors of the economy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are keeping a close watch and will be prepared to respond where needed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While we have made progress in housing, we know that there are some families who may not be able to afford a home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members spoke about this, including Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, and they asked about how we can help these lower-income and vulnerable families.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will exercise flexibility and compassion and do all we can to help the families in need.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those in need of housing, we have ramped up our rental flat supply to ensure that they have a roof over their heads.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to build more rental flats to accommodate this demand.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister of State Koh Poh Koon will say more about this later.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides providing rental flats, we want to do more to help second timers in public rental buy a home.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is aimed at parents with school-going children, so that their children can grow up in a stable home environment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, the families who qualify will be able to buy a new 2-room flexi flat.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The flat will come with shorter leases, ranging from 45 to 65 years, to keep the price affordable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will also come with a longer MOP, I think Mr Gan Thiam Poh also suggested this just now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The longer MOP will be 20 years to ensure a stable home for the children.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will give them another HDB concessionary loan, regardless of the number of HDB loans they have taken before.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They may have taken two loans before from HDB, but we will give these families another HDB concessionary loan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They can use their CPF for the downpayment and also for the mortgage payments.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The amount of grant will be prorated according to the lease of the flat they buy.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together, I believe these measures provide significant help for second-timer families in rental flats to own their own home again.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The scheme is not just about buying a new flat, but also about integrating financial assistance with personal responsibility and social support.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To qualify for the scheme and receive the full grant, families will have to show commitment to remain in stable employment, manage their finances well and ensure their children are attending school regularly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are conditions that we have worked out through our consultations, and they were also highlighted by several Members, including Mr Alex Yam, earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I want to assure Members that our approach is one where we will handhold the families closely and walk this journey with them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If along the way, some families encounter difficulties, the social agencies will be there to help them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will consider their individual circumstances and the effort that they are making to meet the conditions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We hope this approach will keep the families motivated, so that they can make the most of this opportunity to get a fresh start and own their own homes again.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How will the Fresh Start Scheme help a rental family?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the slide are Mr and Mrs Tan.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They have a son and are now staying in a rental flat paying rental of $240 a month.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is slightly more than their monthly rental.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the key is this: they can now pay for this largely through their CPF.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Not all of them may choose to take up the scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will depend on their individual finances and circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The numbers may not be very big, but I believe the scheme can and will have a meaningful impact on the families that we are reaching out to.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is our first priority on home ownership and the different ways in which we are strengthening home ownership.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our next priority is to transform our urban landscape and build our city for the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the last 50 years, we have succeeded in making Singapore a modern global city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We had bold and innovative plans for urban renewal.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We did it through systematic implementation over many terms of Government.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must consider how we want to build our future city over the next 50 years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In some ways, it will be a more difficult journey because we are starting from a higher base with more biting resource constraints.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are in a new era of city competition.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are more than 400 cities in the world, each with at least a million people.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Among them are many emerging world cities, all vying for talent and investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are starting from a higher base, but we cannot afford to stand still.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We should take comfort that we are moving from a position of strength.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Despite our limitation of size, we are far from saturation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are still many possibilities for urban development and transformation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Members will know that we are consolidating our port at Tuas, and this would free up more land for redevelopment at the Greater Southern waterfront.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That parcel there is about three times the size of Marina Bay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am not saying that we are going to build three Marina Bays there, but it is to give a context that it is three times the size of Marina Bay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are expanding Changi Air Hub with a new Terminal 5 and relocating Paya Lebar over at Changi.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, this will free up 800 hectares of prime land for mixed-use development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, in comparison, that is equivalent to half a Jurong Industrial estate, one Ang Mo Kio Town and two Tampines Regional Centres.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am not saying we are going to do that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But this is the perspective of what kind of scale we have, and the mix of uses can vary because we have to plan and think through what plans we want to do with this land that is freed up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the next 10-20 years, we will be building up several regional nodes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have the second central business district (CBD) at Jurong Lake District which will also be the site for the high-speed rail terminus to Kuala Lumpur.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have a new Creative Cluster at Punggol, together with the new Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) campus.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have a new Northern Growth corridor at Woodlands and Sembawang, with many opportunities to transform the waterfront for new jobs and homes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also looking at new and innovative infrastructure solutions, for example, exploring autonomous vehicles, infrastructure needed for driverless cars, smart power grids and underground options for electrical substations and drainage reservoir systems.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is a lot to do, there is a lot of potential for us to move forward and we are studying all of these ideas in the Committee on the Future Economy, in particular, in the subcommittee on the Future City which I co-chair.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also planning ahead for our HDB towns and estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the early years, priority was just to get the blocks of HDB flats completed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But over the years, much more attention has been paid on planning the entire HDB town − the amenities and facilities that come with it, as well as ensuring that there is access to greenery and public spaces.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Planning work is not easy, but we are trying very hard to have a range of facilities and shops in our housing estates ready when residents move in.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB will ensure that there will always be some shops built in tandem with new flats, so that residents will always have access to some facilities, greenery and public spaces.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But development plans that are based on assumptions may not always pan out or the assumptions may not always pan out, or they may take time to be staged.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is easy to criticise our civil servants for "poor town planning", as Mr Dennis Tan said earlier in the Budget debate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I think that is not being fair to them and the work that they do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the end of the day, what is important is the ability to continually update our urban plans to keep pace with the needs of society.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the approach we take in our HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For existing towns, we are continually upgrading and rejuvenating them through various upgrading programmes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Senior Minister of State Desmond Lee will elaborate on them later.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For new housing areas, we learn from our past experience, and we are developing HDB estates and towns with distinctive character.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We pay attention to the history and heritage of the place, we provide for beautiful greenery, beautiful blue spaces, and neighbourhood amenities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we can see these in all our new projects, be it in Bidadari, Punggol or Tampines North.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is next to the Jurong Innovation District.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will be integrated with nature and also the nearby Jurong Innovation District.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am not going to do an extended sales pitch here in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Members can see a picture of what Tengah can be.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have seen many more plans, pictures and visualisations of what our planners are doing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think it will be a very exciting place to live, work and play.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB will release more details in due course.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But they are, first and foremost, places where people meet, interact and connect with one another.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is even more important for us in Singapore, where we only have one city, which is our country and our home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As we transform our city, we must make this place more sustainable, more beautiful and more invigorating to the human spirit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we emphasised clean and green from the outset, and we are making progress as a City in a Garden.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In our next phase, we must focus on our public spaces, streets, squares and footpaths.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must make sure that these developments, these public spaces, are well designed, they relate to the human scale and are well-connected and conducive for walking and cycling.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members, including Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Darryl David and Mr Louis Ng spoke about this, and I fully share their views.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am also glad that Mr Saktiandi Supaat shared the example of the Novena Health City.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think this is one area which we have planned for a comprehensive coverage of underground pedestrian links, street-level walkways and elevated link-bridges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a good example of what we are striving to achieve.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Indeed, we have similar plans for other areas too – in the CBD, Jurong Lake District and all our regional centres.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This new requirement will make sure that developers incorporate the needs of pedestrians and cyclists upfront in their development plans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, developers will have to review the locations of the vehicular access points to minimise conflict with pedestrians and cyclists, taking into account key pedestrian and cyclist access routes and the location of bicycle parking facilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is especially critical for developments with high footfall like our schools, shopping malls, office buildings and business parks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Through these requirements, we will ensure that our built environment is more conducive for pedestrians and cyclists.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides new developments, I agree with Mr Ang Wei Neng that we need to do more for greater connectivity in existing buildings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, I am not sure if Mr Ang heard this earlier, because we had a debate when Dr Tan Wu Meng moved an Adjournment Motion on this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I had shared earlier in the House that we are studying and reviewing legislation to allow us to mandate existing developments to receive new elevated and underground links.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Once this is in place, we plan to get more pedestrian connections along Orchard Road and other areas as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: What do we hope to achieve with all of these changes?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: How can we be a better, more attractive city for walking and cycling?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, within every HDB estate, we will have more dedicated paths for active mobility, be it walking, jogging, cycling or the use of other personal mobility devices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will enhance our first-mile/last-mile connectivity to MRT stations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our newer housing areas, such as Bidadari, Punggol and Tampines North, are already designed with these paths.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For existing towns, we will progressively improve the infrastructure through our upgrading programmes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will allow better connectivity to MRT stations, major employment areas, parks, schools as well as the Neighbourhood Centres.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Intra-HDB towns, new ones, we will do it upfront; existing ones, we will do so through upgrading progressively.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will have a very well-connected route of dedicated walking, cycling paths within each HDB town.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Next, we will also have active mobility routes that connect our residential towns to our city centre.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will enable people to get to their workplaces without having to drive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These cover connections from towns and estates in various regions: from the east, such as Geylang and Marine Parade; northeast, such as Hougang and Macpherson; and the west, such as Queenstown and Bukit Merah.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These routes are largely already in place today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are not new routes because they are largely in place today through our Park Connectors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I give an example of the Bishan to City route which runs along the Kallang River.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, if you take that route, as a cyclist or jogger, you will have to traverse several pedestrian overhead bridges and underpasses, and the biggest obstacle is that you have to cross the Pan Island Expressway (PIE).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is very difficult if you want to cycle down that route to the city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: You have to dismount, go up the pedestrian overhead bridge, underpass, and then you have to find some way to get round the PIE.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, this is just one possibility of how something can be done to bridge the gap.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The picture on screen shows a bridge across Serangoon Road, a potential bridge that you can cycle through.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, if we are able to smoothen out these different kinks in the route, say, with potential links like this, then residents staying in Bishan, Bidadari, Toa Payoh would have a more direct and seamless travelling experience, whether it is through walking, cycling or any other personal mobility device, from their HDB towns to the city centre.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is an example, conceptually, of what we are looking at, how we can enhance connections from HDB towns to the city centre.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also look at active mobility routes within the city centre itself.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And here we can have potential for wider pedestrian sidewalks and dedicated cycling and walking paths as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These will connect to the major office developments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of these pathways in Marina Bay have already been implemented and we will continue to do more in other parts of the CBD.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are some of our ideas and plans to make Singapore a more attractive city for walking, cycling and active mobility.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They will seek the public's views on these different active mobility routes and the types of enhancements needed to make them more useful.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The infrastructure is important, but we must certainly go beyond infrastructure planning to embrace a car-lite mindset.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about this and highlighted the need for more basic awareness and education.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: MOT will be sharing more about this in its COS later.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also need strategies to better manage the use of cars.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One way is to facilitate more car sharing schemes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It can be through electric vehicles (EVs), as suggested by Mr Ong Teng Koon.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our agencies are studying this, as well as the charging infrastructure that may be needed to facilitate the take-up of such EVs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Car park charges are another important lever that we can use.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I know Mr Lim Biow Chuan has called for more free parking in car parks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Free parking is a subsidy to the motorists that is paid for by non-motorists.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, our car park charges are generally lower than most other major cities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the specific concerns raised by Mr Lim Biow Chuan are, I think, about the availability of lots which are being used up for commercial vehicles today, or it is really about how we can provide for more lots for commercial vehicles in residential areas, so that they will not have to park next to his residents' homes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have to look at that more specifically and find other ways to address this issue.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we have started by pedestrianising our vehicular roads, where possible, to create car-free zones, be it on weekends or even on a permanent basis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is our attempt to show how car-free streets can become attractive public spaces for all to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, we have had two editions of it so far.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have it at the Civic District and the CBD area and there has been a tremendous response to this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also expanding car-free zones to streets all over Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are marked out in the map, in addition to our car-free zones on Sunday.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With more support from the community, we can do more in other areas as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, recently, additional roads have been closed for car-free events – Jalan Pisang, Keong Saik Road and Armenian Street.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to do more, not just in the city but also beyond the city, so that we can have more pedestrianised and car-free zones in our HDB estates as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: How do we decide which roads to close or which streets to activate?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is really based on ground-up feedback and proposals.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, I visited Kampong Glam recently on one of the car-free weekends, trying to revisit my childhood with the kids skipping.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think I can still keep up with the kids because if you look at the picture, I am the one who is jumping among the highest.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a completely ground-up initiative by the business owners and stakeholders in the area.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a completely ground-up initiative by the stakeholders there, the business owners.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They decided to do it and URA supported them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The business owners reported an increase in sales due to higher footfall and the public also enjoyed the bustling street life.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to support more of such ground-up initiatives, not only to activate our streets, but also our public spaces in the city and in our HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will strengthen our sense of ownership, identity and emotional connection to home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: People are always at the centre of our policies, be it our housing programme, our urban transformation plans or our initiatives for more vibrant public spaces.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: People are also a critical factor in the success of our policies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we want Singaporeans to be actively involved in shaping our policies and our future city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Taking ownership of the spaces we live in is what makes a house a home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
