text: Therefore, we require a multi-pronged and a multi-agency approach to help them get to the root of the problem.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Housing is perhaps one of them; it could be just the surface and the symptom.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We want to help them get on with their lives again by solving the problem at its root.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As for the 30-month debarment that Mr Faisal Manap said earlier, HDB takes a very flexible approach, and will look at this on a case by case basis to make sure that none of our residents is disadvantaged and has no roof over their heads.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about how we help single parents with housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We can do so in a few ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some Members will know this as the Assistance Scheme for Second-Timers (ASSIST).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Thirdly, we can offer them temporary housing at below market rates while they await completion of their flat, under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS) or in Interim Rental Housing.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Lastly, if they have no housing options and no family support, we will enable them to rent a rental flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap asked whether we can help elderly flat owners who want to rent out a room to find a tenant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We interviewed about 1,200 elderly flat owners on subletting a few years ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Among those who did not rent out their flats or rooms, only 5% of those interviewed had genuine concerns about finding a tenant.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And in actual fact, tenant-matching is already offered by estate agents and various websites.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On HDB's part, we have made the procedure to rent out a room very straightforward.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Owners just need to register with HDB within seven days of finding a tenant for the room that they are letting out.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will monitor the response to LBS further before considering any extension to larger flat types.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But let me emphasise that LBS is not the only option to monetise a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Elderly households staying in larger flats, for example, 5-room flats, actually have a few options to monetise their flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By doing so and staying in a short-lease 2-room flexi flat, they can also benefit from the Silver Housing Bonus which is a cash bonus.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Thirdly, for those who have moved in with their children to enjoy mutual support, they can also consider renting out the whole flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These are all good ways to monetise a flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In answer to Mr Chen Show Mao's question earlier about LBS, I think there are many options other than LBS in which the flat owner can monetise the flat, especially if the flat owner or the elderly couple has the desire to pass the flat on to their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Monetising their flats in ways other than LBS will be an option for them to consider.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The take-up of these monetising schemes is not a numbers game.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There is no key performance indicator to meet, to see how many people should monetise their flats.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They are options for the elderly to consider to suit their needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, many elderly today have personal savings and support from their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They may not feel a need to monetise their flat.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, HDB continues to publicise monetisation options through various means, through its website, local media, public talks, exhibitions and at enquiry booths at community events.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Interested flat owners can approach HDB and be given one-to-one advice on how they can monetise their flats based on their individual needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond housing, MND also oversees the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority (AVA), which has a wide scope, ranging from managing animals to ensuring Singapore's food security.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA manages stray dogs, cats and wild monkeys to address feedback on public concerns caused by the animals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA's contractors are required to have the necessary expertise and comply with animal welfare guidelines in handling these animals.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I also want to reassure Members that we take all animal cruelty cases seriously.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA will investigate feedback on animal cruelty and welfare issues and take the wrongdoers to task.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Louis Ng has asked about collaboration between AVA and animal welfare groups (AWGs) on animal-related issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For instance, the Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES) is one of AVA's contractors for responding to wild animal issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA also works with the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) and the Cat Welfare Society (CWS) on the Stray Cat Sterilisation Programme (SCSP).

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under the programme, AVA co-funds the cost of sterilising and micro-chipping stray cats in HDB estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The AWGs also help to mediate cat-related feedback and manage community cat feeders to prevent nuisance to the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AWGs play a very important intermediary role in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Going forward, AVA will expand the programme to cover stray cats in industrial and commercial areas, and private estates.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA also works closely with AWGs on public outreach regarding animal-related issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through the Responsible Pet Ownership Programme, AVA has held roadshows and joint adoption drives with AWGs, emphasising that a pet is for life and should not be abandoned.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA plans to collaborate with AWGs to further such outreach efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Besides AWGs, AVA also works with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) and Singapore Customs (SC) to clamp down on illegal wildlife trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: AVA also works closely with international partners, such as wildlife authorities in ASEAN countries and the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL), to deter such illegal animal trade.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With the support of these partners, I would like to assure Mr Louis Ng that AVA will remain vigilant and continue to optimise resources to tackle animal issues and animal crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Alex Yam spoke about the need to transform our local agriculture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Climate change, whether it is global warming or irregular weather patterns, is causing greater uncertainties in overseas food supply.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At the same time, the world population is growing, projected to increase from 7.3 billion today to 9.7 billion by 2050.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through our Agriculture Productivity Fund, we will continue to provide financial support to promising farmers in adopting these technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will create the right environment where our farmers can grow more with less, through the use of technology and innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to show some visuals on the LED screens, please?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We envision that farms of the future will make use of integrated vertical and indoor systems, automation and robotics.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They will be highly intensive and productive and operate on minimal manpower.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are already beginning to see this new breed of farms in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Just last month, I visited Apollo Aquarium and Sky Greens, which represent state-of-the-art urban and vertical farming technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Apollo Aquarium houses its fish in indoor, vertical multi-tiered tanks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They use less land, yet produce more fish.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In a controlled environment, the farm can be monitored and operated remotely, without the risks of uncontrollable environmental factors that can threaten the yield of the fish stock.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Sky Greens is the world's first commercial vertical farm.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Its three-storey-high vertical racks can produce about 2,500 stalks of vegetables.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This system requires less water, less electricity and less labour, yet produces five times more leafy vegetables than traditional farms.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Across the board, local production levels for our key food items, such as food fish, leafy vegetables and hen's eggs, have steadily risen over the years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Imagine what we can achieve if all our local farmers employ these technologies!

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We may become much more self-sufficient in some of our essential food items.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To realise their full potential, besides adopting transformative technologies, there is scope for the agricultural sector to consolidate and intensify their operations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will move the needle in production and in their manpower optimisation strategy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have a mission to achieve that is as crucial as water and that is to strengthen our food security in an era of global food uncertainty.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: My Ministry and AVA will make the development of our local agricultural sector a priority for the coming years.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I do have a little bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I want to remind Members that clarifications are for clarifications and not to make speeches, and to ask clarifications relating to the Minister's answers only.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I have a clarification for the Minister with regard to the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The reason behind it is that if you set it at 20 years, it means that the average age of families who are entering this scheme would mean that most of them would not be able to move to a bigger flat by the time they hit the 20 years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: The second clarification is about the 1,000 families that the Minister mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: This seems to be a small proportion of the total number families.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Would this scheme be incremental after the first pilot?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Lastly, for large families, the 2-room flexi flats are a little bit small.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Would the Ministry consider any flexibility in this area?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I understand the Member's concern with regard to the size of the flat, the MOP requirement and also the number of potential beneficiaries of Fresh Start.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I would just highlight that when we thought about the scheme and we looked at the potential beneficiaries, the profile I was talking about, second-timers in rental flats with young children, school-going children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you look at the savings and the balances they have today, there is an affordability issue even if we, say, buy a 3-room flat now, even with the grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not going to be so easy for them to do so.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have to be realistic about what they can afford.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even after the Fresh Start grant, given the balances that they have in savings and the situation they are in, I think it is more realistic to aim for a 2-room flexi flat for a start.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the longer MOP is there to make sure that there is a stable environment for the children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Should any of these families who apply, eventually down the road, say that they have been able to be successful, with better incomes and now are better able to afford a 3-room flat, I think we can facilitate that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even if it is within the MOP, we will find ways to facilitate that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because that is a success story which we should celebrate; meaning this is a household which came under Fresh Start, got a 2-room flat, and then said, now we have succeeded, incomes are stabilised, are better, we are able to afford a 3-room flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we wanted the long MOP to make sure that there is stability for the home environment and also to avoid situations where families cash out their flats early.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: I want to clarify that the Town Council does have a regular maintenance regime for the lifts.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: What we found out is that the breakdown or failure of the parts are unusually fast, compared to some other lifts.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The question then is what is the quality of the LUP lifts?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: What are the safeguards or specifications that HDB has got, in terms of the tender?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: On the issue of lift market, maintenance market, I understand that the new lift being installed with the manufacturing company will come with its own motherboard, which other companies will not be able to maintain.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Which means that, going forward, the Town Council's lift maintenance will be held ransom by this manufacturing company.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The fundamental question is what is the situation of the lift manufacture and maintenance market in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Is the market competitive or are we in a situation where you have not much of choice, but are dependent on these companies?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Will they decide how much they will increase the price in maintenance every year?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: Of course, probably Opposition Town Councils will be at a disadvantage, because we are not given the leeway of discounts, as they give to PAP Town Councils, from what I know.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the issue of lift breakdowns, the Member talks about the quality of LUP.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, there are certain specifications that have to be met.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, I think we need to really have a proper drill down by the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you think there is an issue, raise it to MND and HDB, so that you can assess whether it is an issue of the lift brand, lift model, or is it a specific issue with regard to a particular shaft.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I think beyond speculation, it is better to look at specifics.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The hon Member also speaks about motherboards of lifts and that, therefore, he is concerned about whether there is market competitiveness with regard to maintenance of lifts in HDB estates, which responsibilities then fall on Town Councils across the island.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said earlier, there are many players in the lift supply market and the lift maintenance market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, Mr Low Thia Khiang talked about the manufacturer then having proprietary ownership in the technology of the motherboards, but there are also other parts of the lifts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each of these lift maintenance companies, whether they are manufacturer or third-party contractor, comes in variant profiles and capabilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There may be more complex maintenance issues which may require certain parties with specific competencies, such as the original lift manufacturer, to resolve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If there are any concerns that the Member raises, please let us know specifically, whether the motherboard, the type he is concerned about, let us know.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, I just wanted to add in response to Mr Low Thia Khiang's query, as I understand his suggestion is to look at how we can standardise more components within the lifts.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One, to bring down costs, and secondly, so that we will not be held hostage or the Town Councils will not be held hostage by any particular Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The objectives that we have are, indeed, aligned, because we have, over the years, been doing more standardisation.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why, in the early days, all the lift maintenance contracts were done by OEMs entirely.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We were in a very difficult situation where we had to pay whatever prices that the OEMs charged.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are third-party contractors, but Mr Low Thia Khiang is right, that not everything can be done by the third-party contractor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Sometimes, for very complex things, for certain parts, you still need to go to the OEM.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We should try and aim for an even more competitive market, so I agree with the Member.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With just one caveat, that we have to study this very carefully, because this is quite complex.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If we were to overly prescribe certain standards, and say only these things can be done, we may end up with a situation where we limit our choices that we have to purchase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Fewer OEMs will bid for lift contracts in Singapore, the cost may be higher.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is complex and we have to look at this in detail.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I would say that the direction of what the Member has suggested is something we agree with.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB has already done this and we will continue to do more of it.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The main point of the cut is that under the current scheme, the repair is only being done to the upper floor.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Basically, there is an issue of leakage, so repair work will be done on the floor of the upper floor unit, the source of the leak.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: But due to the leak, it damages the lower floor's ceiling.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, the repair of this damaged ceiling is not covered under the Goodwill Repair Assistance scheme.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: The feedback that I have got from those living on the lower floor units is that they wonder why they should pay a share of the repair done on the upper floor.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Chairman, the Goodwill Repair Assistance scheme involves HDB coming in to help facilitate the resolution of maintenance issues faced by both upper and lower floors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Most of the work, as the Member rightly points out, involves waterproofing membrane works for the upper floor unit.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For the lower floor unit, you may need to fix some spalling of concrete, because of the leakage problem.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the Goodwill Repair Assistance scheme also addresses that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For the Member's particular case, let us have a closer look and we will see what aspect of the ceiling has been damaged and whether it is related to the leakage.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The Minister mentioned that it will be cleared soon.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The second question is on the Fresh Start Grant.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The Minister mentioned that they should have school-going age children.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The third question is on the construction industry.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We would not be able to exactly pinpoint what is the demand from singles, because there may be more coming forward to apply.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not have the exact number in terms of forecasting demand from singles, but I would say that it is still quite strong.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We still see quite a lot of applications even in the last BTO exercise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you look at the application rate, as I mentioned, it is more than seven, which indicates that there is still very strong demand.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Will even more come forward once the queue gets shorter?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why I said even after we have cleared this current surge of demand, there may be more coming forward, but that is the kind of numbers and timeframe we are looking at.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The second question is on the Fresh Start Grant and the condition for the school-going children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are looking at a parent with at least one child in school, particularly because we want to make sure that the child has a stable environment to grow up in.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if they have more than one child, they can be in university, they can be in tertiary institutions, private institutions, and that is fine.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Chairman, may I deal with the Member's last question, which is on whether BCA is doing anything to encourage the growth of the Singapore Core with regard to the built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I presume the Member is talking about architects, consultants, designers and contractors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I spoke earlier in my speech about how BCA is going upstream and having a whole suite of scholarships to encourage Singapore students in our institutions, whether it is in ITE, polytechnics and universities, to come onboard the built environment sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is also an Earn-and-Learn scheme, where after they join the particular programme at an institution, they learn and earn along the way and get brought into the sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, whilst the push to productivity is one of the key drivers behind adopting higher technology or game-changing technology in construction, such as VDC and DfMA, ultimately, if you look at it, by using technology, using ICT, building in a smart and creative way, this also creates niches and opportunities for Singaporeans to come into the built environment sector as well.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Chairman, I would like to seek a clarification from the Senior Minister of State whether the Ministry will consider reviewing or removing the terms and conditions of the land sales, such as specifying the method of construction, which has an effect on increasing development cost?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think we all agree as to the direction.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member is concerned about whether these actually achieve the objectives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The objective is the same but, on the methods, we might have a slight difference of opinion.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think it is about 60% by PPVC; the rest can be by casting in situ; so, we provide some flexibility.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is transparent and it is a level-playing field.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Parties who bid for these land sale sites know that there is a certain technological requirement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These help create lead demand for us to adopt the higher productivity methods.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for one of the points, the Member raised in his speech earlier about whether we can relax the requirement for contractors or developers to finish the project within x number of years, I think we do not want the land to be hoarded.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are certain requirements that drive us to have GLS, especially for residential and commercial uses.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are meant to meet the demand that we have projected and we do not want and, certainly, no Singaporean would want land to be hoarded indefinitely.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We want to see that the project is developed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The timeline that URA provides is a reasonable one.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: One, I am happy to hear of the exciting vision to ensure food security.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Dr Koh mentioned a review on the land lease for agricultural land.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Would the Minister of State be able to share when this information will be made available and whether any criteria will be put in place for any longer leases?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: I wonder if the schemes that the Minister of State had mentioned earlier are sufficient to prepare us for any future major downturns.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his clarification questions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First of all, on the issue of land and farming, we obviously want to encourage our farmers to be more productive.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is something that we want to encourage them to do, and the Agricultural Productivity Fund is one of those measures.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will continue to engage our farmers actively to encourage them to do so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As for the question about whether the current schemes and measures are sufficient to help families in the economic downturn, there are quite a number of schemes and policies that can help families, whether they are first-timers, second-timers or divorced.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will see how these schemes can be enhanced or if there is any new scheme that we can introduce to plug the gap.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Chairman, Sir, I just want to clarify the issue I brought up about the LUP design in Hougang, that I have met HDB.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some of the issues have been resolved and some have not because some of them, like the lift-landing breach, HDB said it meets statutory requirements.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Like I said in my cut, because of the proximity to the resident's house and the dry riser, nothing else can be done.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think what is important is to just let us have the details and then we will look into that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I cannot address it here in this Chamber.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Leon Perera, did you want to raise a clarification?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The anecdotal feedback I have from residents —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Perera, please state the clarification and not make a speech.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, my question is: would the Minister of State consider doing this survey on a regular basis?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Because my understanding is that the market has softened and the markets do go through cycles.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, would such a survey about whether flat owners have difficulties finding tenants, be something that the Ministry would do on a regular basis?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The second point of clarification is regarding LBS.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The hon Minister of State mentioned rental and downgrading as other options but, of course, rental depends on the market; downgrading has other downsides, like commissions and costs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: There is evidence to suggest that the bequeath motives hold back some people from exercising LBS.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Would the Ministry look into ways to address the bequeath motive issue that is holding back some people from making use of LBS, such as the suggestion made by Mr Chen Show Mao?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Lastly, on APF, I would like to ask the Ministry why the disbursement of the fund has been quite low so far.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Clearly, there are deserving projects, in terms of indoor and vertical farming.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Is it because of a lack of deserving projects?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Or is it because of some lack of connectivity between the companies, the farmers, and the agency in charge of disbursing the fund?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, for the first question that the Member raised about the rental survey, we all do our Meet-the-People Sessions (MPS), we have residents coming to see us and telling us their issues.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One of the ways we can sense whether this is going to become an important issue is through our MPS.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We can sense whether this is a common enough problem.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But with or without a survey, estate agents are available, websites that allow matching of rental tenants and people with rooms to rent are also available.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we do not quite need a survey for any of these services to be available.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, those who need this can avail themselves of these presently available services right now.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the second question on LBS and whether bequeathing is one of those things that holds people back from taking part in LBS, I think, at the end of the day, it is an option and a choice that the elderly couple has to decide, how they want to monetise their flat.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If they do want to bequeath their flat, then I think it makes more sense for them to retain the whole flat, rent it out in the meantime – either whole flat or a room – while keeping the full intact value of the flat to bequeath it to their children.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If you have an LBS where you already sold part of the lease back to HDB and you only have such a short lease left, I am not sure how much value there is for the couple to bequeath to their children.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If the intent is to bequeath the flat to their children, they should keep the flat.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But if what they want is to monetise their flat, there are many options.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are not trying to push people to go onto LBS, so there is no real need to try to make it so attractive for people to go onto LBS.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Regarding APF and why the take-up rate may not be as high as we would want it to be, part of the reason could be that farmers make their choices about how they want to transform.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have to do it from two ways.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One, encourage them to continue to look forward, to be more forward-looking and to adopt technology.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have come to the end of clarification time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Alex Yam, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: With this all-rounded responsibility, MND and its eight statutory boards have their work cut out.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
